questions.question: Who was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to start military expeditions into southern India?
questions.solution:
• Alauddin Khilji (1296-1316) was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to start military expeditions into southern India.
  • He was the second ruler of the Khilji dynasty.

questions.question: Which monument of Khilji dynasty in Delhi has the utilization of red sandstone?
questions.solution:
• Alai Darwaza, built by Allauddin Khilji in 1311 AD, utilized red sandstone.
  • Moti Masjid was built by Aurangzeb in Delhi.
  • Victoria Memorial was built by George V in Kolkata.
  • Charminar was built by Mohammed Quli Qutub Shah in Hyderabad.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Shahna-i-Mandi was the officer responsible for maintaining a register of merchants to ensure adequate supply of goods.
2. Alauddin Khilji established only one central market in Delhi, where all commodities were sold together.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Shahna-i-Mandi was the officer responsible for maintaining a register of merchants to ensure adequate supply of goods.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: Alauddin Khilji established three markets at Delhi - for food grains, for cloth and daily-use goods, and for horses, slaves, and cattle.

questions.question: How many types of taxes were in the reign of the ruler Alauddin Khilji?
questions.solution:
• There were 3 types of taxes during Alauddin Khilji's reign:
  • Jaziya - religious tax on the Hindu community
  • Ghari tax - tax on houses
  • Chari tax - tax on cattle

questions.question: The Begumpuri mosque was built during the reign of which of the following rulers of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
• The Begumpuri mosque was built during the reign of Muhammad Tughlaq.
  • He was the eighteenth Sultan of Delhi, ruling from February 1324 to 1351.
  • He was the eldest son of Ghiyath al-Din Tughlaq, founder of the Tughlaq dynasty.
  • He built the Begumpur Mosque (Jami Masjid of Jahanpanah) in the capital, Jahanpanah.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first sultan of Delhi Sultanate to visit the Ajmer shrine of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti?
questions.solution:
• Muhammad bin Tughlaq, originally known as Junakhan, ascended the throne in 1324.
  • He was the first sultan of the Delhi Sultanate to visit the Ajmer shrine of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti.
  • In 1327 AD, he successfully captured Warangal, a significant event in his reign.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Muhammad Tughlaq founded the Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi.
2. The Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was established mainly to strengthen the army.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Muhammad Tughlaq set up the Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: It was established to bring more land under cultivation, not to strengthen the army.
  • He also promoted agriculture by reducing agrarian cesses and providing agricultural loans called Sondhar.

questions.question: Which amongst the following Sultans shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?
questions.solution:
• Muhammad Bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to the more centrally located Devagiri in Maharashtra, which was renamed Daulatabad.
  • His five disastrous projects were:
    • Taxation in the Doab
    • Transfer of Capital
    • Khurasan Expedition
    • Qarachil Expedition
    • Introduction of Token Currency

questions.question: Who invaded India during the rule of Tughlaq Dynasty?
questions.solution:
• During the reign of Nasir-ud-din Mahmud Tughlaq, Timur invaded India in 1398 AD.
  • This invasion led to the decline of the Tughlaq dynasty.

questions.question: Which of the following cities of Delhi was founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq?
questions.solution:
• Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq (reign: 1320-1324) founded the city of Tughlaqabad.
  • He was the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty (1320-1414 AD), the longest-ruling dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.
  • City and founder:
    • Siri - Alauddin Khilji
    • Jahanpanah - Muhammad bin Tughlaq
    • Qila-i-Rai Pithora - Prithviraj Chauhan

questions.question:
Arrange the following rulers of the Tughlaq dynasty in chronological order:
1. Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq
2. Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq
3. Firuz Shah Tughlaq
questions.solution:
• The correct chronological order is: Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq (1320-1325) → Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq (1325-1351) → Firuz Shah Tughlaq (1351-1388).
  • The Tughlaq dynasty was founded by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq.
  • Firuz Shah Tughlaq is remembered for irrigation works, Diwan-i-Khairat, and other welfare measures.

questions.question: Who amongst the following raised the banner of revolt against Nasiruddin Khusrau?
questions.solution:
• Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq (or Ghazi Malik, 1320-1324 AD) raised the banner of revolt against Nasiruddin Khusrau.
  • He was the governor of Punjab during the reign of Alauddin Khilji.
  • He was the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty, fought against the Mongols, and started the construction of Tughlaqabad Fort.

questions.question: The author of Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi, Yahya Sirhindi claims that the founder of ______ dynasty of Delhi sultanate was a descendant of Prophet Muhammad.
questions.solution:
• Yahya Sirhindi claims that the founder of the Sayyid dynasty was a descendant of Prophet Muhammad.
  • Khizr Khan defeated Sultan Daulat Khan, occupied Delhi, and founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1414.
  • Capital: Delhi.
  • Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi contains the history of Muhammad Ghori and his rulers up to the third ruler of the Sayyid dynasty.

questions.question:
Arrange the following rulers of the Sayyid Dynasty in chronological order:
1. Alauddin Alam Shah
2. Khizr Khan
3. Mubarak Shah
4. Muhammad Shah
questions.solution:
• The correct chronological order is: Khizr Khan (1414-1421) → Mubarak Shah (1421-1434) → Muhammad Shah (1434-1445) → Alauddin Alam Shah (1445-1451).
  • Khizr Khan was the founder of the Sayyid dynasty.
  • Mubarak Shah constructed Mubarakbad city and appointed Hindu nobles in his court.
  • Alauddin Alam Shah was the last ruler, who surrendered Delhi to Bahlul Lodi in 1451.

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate finally annexed Jaunpur into the empire of Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
• The Lodi dynasty was founded by Bahlol Lodi, the last ruling dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate (1451-1526).
  • In AD 1476, Bahlol Lodi defeated the Sultan of Jaunpur and annexed it to the Delhi Sultanate.
  • He also brought the ruler of Kalpi and Dholpur under the suzerainty of Delhi.

questions.question: Who among the following was the last sultan of Delhi sultanate?
questions.solution:
• Ibrahim Lodi was the last Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate (1206-1526).
  • He became Sultan in 1517 after the death of his father Sikandar Khan Lodi.
  • In 1526, he was defeated and killed in the First Battle of Panipat by Babur, giving way to the emergence of the Mughal Empire in India.

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties of Delhi Sultanate founded Agra city?
questions.solution:
• The Lodi dynasty (1451-1526) founded Agra city.
  • It was founded by Bahlul Lodi (1451-1489 AD).
  • Sultan Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504.
  • Famous historic cities and their founders:
    • Fatehpur Sikri (Uttar Pradesh) - Akbar
    • Hampi (Karnataka) - Harihara I and Bukka Raya I
    • Udaipur (Rajasthan) - Udai Singh II
    • Warangal (Telangana) - Kakatiya dynasty

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding mosques of Delhi Sultanate:
1. Moth ki Masjid in Delhi was built during the Lodi dynasty.
2. Begumpuri Mosque in Delhi was constructed during the reign of the Lodis.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Moth ki Masjid was built in 1505 by Wazir Miya Bhoiya during the Lodi dynasty.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: Begumpuri Mosque was constructed under Muhammad bin Tughlaq, not the Lodis.

questions.question: 'Double Dome' feature of Indo-Islamic architecture was introduced by which dynasty of Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
• The 'Double Dome' feature was introduced by the Lodi Dynasty (1451-1526).
  • Double dome consists of two layers: an inner layer providing a ceiling to the interior, and an outer layer crowning the building.
  • Example: Humayun's Tomb.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Sharqi dynasty:
1. The dynasty was founded by Khwajah-i-Jahan Malik Sarwar in 1394.
2. The Sharqi dynasty ruled over the Agra Sultanate.
3. The dynasty came to an end after the defeat of Sultan Hussain Shah by Bahlul Lodi in 1479.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: The Sharqi dynasty was founded by Khwajah-i-Jahan Malik Sarwar in 1394.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The Sharqi dynasty ruled the Jaunpur Sultanate, not Agra.
  • Statement 3 is correct: The dynasty ended after Sultan Hussain Shah Sharqi was defeated by Bahlul Lodi in 1479.

questions.question: How did the administrative roles of rajas differ from those of zamindars under the Mughal system?
questions.option_1: Zamindars were subordinate tax officers under the rajas, appointed directly by the emperor.
questions.option_2: Rajas and zamindars performed identical roles but differed in their religious affiliations.
questions.option_3: Rajas governed broader regions and held a higher status, while zamindars primarily managed land revenue collection.
questions.option_4: Zamindars exercised complete political control, whereas rajas held only ceremonial titles.
questions.solution:
• Under the Mughal administrative system, rajas (especially Rajput rulers and other local kings) governed large territories and had higher political status.
  • Zamindars were land revenue collectors and intermediaries who managed smaller areas, often villages or clusters of villages.
  • Zamindars were important for revenue administration but did not hold sovereignty like rajas.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the reason Qandhar was strategically important for the Mughals?
questions.option_1: It provided direct naval access to the Red Sea for Mughal expeditions.
questions.option_2: It served as a religious pilgrimage center linking India with Central Asian Sufi shrines.
questions.option_3: It was a crucial trade hub connecting the Arabian Sea with the Persian Gulf.
questions.option_4: It controlled key land routes between Kabul and Herat and acted as a fortified military outpost.
questions.solution:
• Qandhar (Kandahar, Afghanistan) was a key Mughal frontier controlling routes between Central Asia, Persia, and India.
  • It served as a fortified military outpost and trade gateway.
  • Its strategic value led to repeated Mughal-Safavid conflicts under Akbar, Jahangir, and Shah Jahan.

questions.question: What led to the decline of Timurid power in the second half of the 15th century?
questions.option_1: Economic decline due to maritime trade shifts
questions.solution:
• The Timurid Empire began to weaken in the second half of the 15th century mainly due to the rise of the Uzbeks under Muhammad Shaybani.
  • The Uzbeks consolidated power in Central Asia and displaced the Timurids from Transoxiana (Samarkand and Bukhara).
  • The fall of Timurid authority forced Babur, a Timurid prince, to seek opportunities elsewhere, leading to the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India (1526).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements in the context of the Mughal Rule.
1. The Mansabdari System was introduced by Akbar in 1571.
2. The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556.
3. Maharana Pratap Singh of Mewar was a contemporary of Babur.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Statements 1 and 2 are correct.
  • The Mansabdari System was introduced by Akbar in 1571 as a grading system to rank officers based on their ranks and salaries.
  • The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556 between Akbar and Hemu.
  • Statement 3 is incorrect: Maharana Pratap Singh was a contemporary of Akbar, not Babur. He led Rajput resistance against Akbar at the Battle of Haldighati (1576) and the Battle of Dewair (1582).

questions.question: Who among the following was the guru of Tansen?
questions.solution:
• Swami Haridasa was the guru of Tansen.
  • Tansen was one of the Navratnas (nine gems) in the court of Emperor Akbar, who bestowed the title 'Mian' upon him.
